author: Temminck, 1835
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 겨울철새 수천 마리
summary: 해마다 수만 마리가 지나가고 수천 마리가 겨울을 나는 철새로, 넓은 초지, 습지, 간척 농경지에서 가족 단위로 지내며 이동 시기와 월동지에서는 여러 가족이 모여 큰 무리를 이룬다. 벼를 비롯한 낟알과 식물의 줄기, 뿌리를 먹는다. 러시아 아무르 유역과 중국 북동부에서 번식하고 중국 양쯔강 유역, 일본, 한국에서 겨울을 나며, 국내에서는 주로 순천만과 서산 간척지에서 월동한다.

young: 어린새는 머리와 목이 엷은 황갈색이고 몸은 흑갈색이며, 이마에 검은색이 없다.

art.subject: Hooded Crane (Grus monacha), adult in winter, as seen on Korean reclaimed farmland from October to March: head and upper half of the neck white; forehead and lores black; a small patch of bare red skin on the crown; lower neck, body and wing coverts dark slaty grey; flight feathers blackish; tertials dark grey, slightly drooping over the tail. Pale yellowish bill; blackish legs and feet.
art.pose: feeding on grain in a harvested rice field
art.scene: Korean winter reclaimed farmland and harvested rice fields beside a bay; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing: white head and upper neck, black forehead, small red crown patch, dark slaty-grey lower neck and body, drooping dark tertials over the tail, blackish legs
adult in flight seen from below: neck and legs fully outstretched in a straight line, wings entirely blackish, white head and upper neck
juvenile (first winter), side view standing: head and upper neck pale buff-tinged white with no black forehead or red crown, body blackish-brown
art.build: Small crane, about 100cm, a little taller than a Grey Heron but much bulkier, with a long neck and long legs; walks slowly while feeding in family groups. Head small and rounded. Bill straight and pointed, about as long as the head. Legs long, blackish. At rest the tertials form a dark bustle covering the short tail. In flight the neck and legs are fully outstretched, and the wings look almost entirely blackish.
avoid: Do not paint pink legs, a red face patch or a white stripe down a grey neck — that is White-naped Crane.
Do not paint a white body; the body is dark slaty grey.
Do not show it flying with the neck folded; cranes fly with the neck outstretched.
Do not extend the white down the whole neck; the lower neck is grey.
